import { Aside, Badge, Card, CardGrid, FileTree, Icon, LinkButton, LinkCard, Steps, TabItem, Tabs } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

Everything Starlight gives an author, rendered once each. A token change that looks fine on prose can still break one of these.

## Asides

Both spellings produce the same thing — the directive form works in plain `.md`, the component form only in `.mdx`.

<Aside type="note">Default title, note variant.</Aside>
<Aside type="tip" title="With a custom title">Tip variant.</Aside>
<Aside type="caution">Caution variant.</Aside>
<Aside type="danger" title="Read this one">Danger variant.</Aside>

<Aside type="note" title="Nesting">
An aside can contain a list:

- with items
- and `inline code`

and a fence:

```c
liara_result_t r = liara_init(&desc);
```
</Aside>

## Tabs

Independent:

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="C">

```c
liara_version_t v;
liara_version_current(&v);
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="C++">

```cpp
const auto v = liara::version::current();
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="CMake">

```cmake
find_package(Liara REQUIRED COMPONENTS core)
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Synchronised — picking a tab here switches the group below it too:

<Tabs syncKey="os">
<TabItem label="Linux" icon="linux">Uses `XDG_DATA_HOME`.</TabItem>
<TabItem label="macOS" icon="apple">Uses `~/Library/Application Support`.</TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Tabs syncKey="os">
<TabItem label="Linux" icon="linux">

```bash frame="terminal"
export LIARA_ASSET_ROOT="$XDG_DATA_HOME/liara"
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="macOS" icon="apple">

```bash frame="terminal"
export LIARA_ASSET_ROOT="$HOME/Library/Application Support/liara"
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

## Steps

<Steps>

1. **Write the manifest.** One `dev` version is enough to start.

2. **Write a page.** `docs/index.md` with a `title` in its front matter.

    A step can carry more than one paragraph, and a fence:

    ```bash frame="terminal"
    git add docs/ manifest.json
    ```

3. **Open a pull request** and read the preview.

</Steps>

## Badges

Inline: <Badge text="stable" variant="success" />
<Badge text="preview" variant="note" />
<Badge text="deprecated" variant="caution" />
<Badge text="removed" variant="danger" />
<Badge text="default" />
<Badge text="large" variant="tip" size="large" />

In a table, where they earn their place:

| Version | ABI | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dev` | 0.2.0 | <Badge text="compatible" variant="success" /> |
| `0.2.3` | 0.2.0 | <Badge text="compatible" variant="success" /> |
| `0.1.4` | 0.1.0 | <Badge text="degraded" variant="caution" /> |
| `0.0.1` | — | <Badge text="retired" variant="danger" /> |
